annotations.text:
Lead direction — the receipt.

No app on the market shows its arithmetic. Levels and ZOE give a score you can't question; MyFitnessPal gives a database and 3–5 minutes of work per meal. The gap is a legible answer.

Verdict first, in a human voice. Then the number. The receipt on demand — every line traceable. No rings, streaks or scores.

Type and colour follow the PRD identity: Literata, IBM Plex, deep green.

The prototype is clickable. Try all three chips: the bowl asks one question and branches on the answer; the insulin question is refused; kugel gets an honest 'no verified data'. Show calculation opens the receipt and the tool trace.

Every scenario starts from the same moment of the day — 21 of 54 left — so the answers stay comparable.

All numbers are sample values computed by hand from the seed database — not model output.

Two other directions, low-fi.

B puts the numbers first — honest, but it looks like every tracker people have quit.

C leans into the conversation — the agent is visible, but the receipt and the day fight for room in a chat column.

The lead borrows from both: text-first input from C, the receipt's rigour from B.
